events_since_last: Thursday's design review went badly: Daniel said your section was 'not there yet' in front of the team. You did not ask him for the ten minutes; you wrote the email and deleted it. You stayed until 10pm two nights. You are flat and a bit defensive.
You sketched for five minutes on the tram this morning for the first time in months and it felt good, though you nearly did not mention it. Work is busy.
You managed one evening without beer, using the grounding at bedtime. Last night it rained, you had a nightmare and drank three beers. Karim called again and you did not answer.
You are ready for your third written session, nervous. When you write, you will describe the moment the van came out of the side road and Karim's silence afterwards. Your distress starts around 70.

Claire is sitting next to you. You agreed to try the spoken reliving. Your distress starts at 75, peaks near 90 when you describe Karim not moving, and comes down slowly to about 55 if the therapist paces it well. Once, you feel yourself drifting and go quiet.
You did not send a checking message after Tuesday's meeting, but you asked Faris three times whether Hana seemed upset. You will ask the therapist too, in a roundabout way.

Your experiment: you did not check after two of three meetings. Anxiety went from 8 to 4 within an hour without checking, which surprised you. At Sunday lunch your aunt commented on your weight and you have been replaying it.
You called Nok on Friday and it went well, she was pleased. But last night a song Malee loved came on the radio and you drank more than usual. You are a little ashamed.
You went to see the temple volunteer group but did not sign up; you felt you would be forgetting Malee if you enjoyed it. The tutoring on Saturday went well.

A hard week. Halfway through the session, when asked about the evenings, you say quietly that on the worst nights you think it would be fine not to wake up. You have no plan and would not act, if asked directly.
Exam in two weeks; you have studied maybe three hours in total. Your mother keeps calling about grades. You mention basketball coaching only if asked what you enjoy.
You open the practice library and ask for help with the wheel of life. Your areas end up being work, creativity, family, friends, health and home.
